rationale: status_q is held in the black-box set/reset flop sky_dffsr, so the priority between SN and the combined RN, and the overlap behaviour, cannot be decided.

author_reading.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
author_reading.rationale: sky_dffsr is an unmodelled library flop; its set-versus-clear priority is unknown, and RN combines reset with a functional clear, so the outcome when both assert cannot be decided.

labels.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
labels.rationale: The status flop is an opaque sky_dffsr cell. Its RN is an AND of two raw resets, and SN is a raw async set. Their priority inside the cell and the RN combination cannot be decided from RTL.
labels.detection_gap: The set and reset controls sit on black-box pins, so RDC-026 cannot see the set and reset priority.

labels.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
labels.rationale: The missing cell prevents judgment of set versus clear priority, overlap behavior and release timing. Port names do not establish asynchronous control semantics.
labels.detection_gap: RDC-026 requires a modeled register and asynchronous controls. The defined empty module has no black-box attribute or supplied library model, so it also falls outside the CST-005 trigger.
labels.suspected_flaw: The cell is defined as an empty module without a black-box attribute. Its output is undriven in the literal RTL.

settlement.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
settlement.rationale: Both readers are right on unknown and class. The settler added (* black_box *) to sky_dffsr on line 3, so CST-005 now reports it; this answers B's gap note. RDC-008 (A) cannot fire, because RN is a black-box pin and not a modelled reset root, and RDC-002 is incidental.
